name: Royal Court of Tiébélé
description: In the town of Tiébélé in southern Burkina Faso, the Royal Court is a walled cluster of mud-built huts that has been home to the Kasena rulers since the 16th century. Its walls are covered in bold geometric patterns in black, white and red, each with symbolic meaning. Men raise the buildings, but only the women paint them, passing the knowledge down.
